title: a runner's drive runs the caller's own interpreter
intention: Every runner drive that a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail launches names the interpreter running the inspector (a '{python}' placeholder expanded to sys.executable), never a bare interpreter name resolved from PATH, so a runner that leaves a trail never reads as one that does not because PATH named a stub.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell, clean main ba93cd143: cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_a_failed_run_is_counted.py reds 3/4. The rehearsal runner's drive begins with a bare 'python3', which on Windows is the Microsoft Store stub; it exits 9009 and writes no trail, so the sieve reds a runner that does leave one. That is a false red (Law 8 cares about false greens; a false red still blocks every crossing on the box).
traces_to: ba4166fe51c4 (a-failed-run-is-counted: drive each runner's failure through its own CLI verb); Law 3 (measured by running, so the drive has to actually run); 39eccfbc09aa (moved runners_leave_trails.json out of sieves/).
how: In a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail (inspector.py), the argv comprehension that expands '{scratch}' also expands '{python}' to sys.executable. The rehearsal row in cairn/machines/build_inspector/runners_leave_trails.json changes its first word from 'python3' to '{python}'. The tester row (bin/cairn) is untouched. The proof cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_a_runner_drive_runs_the_callers_interpreter.py carries one tooth per falsifier clause. Stacked on branch sieve-why-39eccfbc09aa, where the runners file now lives.

clauses.claim: no runner drive in cairn/machines/build_inspector/runners_leave_trails.json begins with a bare interpreter name (python, python3, py, or one ending .exe), and the rehearsal runner's drive begins with '{python}'

a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail over a testing runner whose drive is ['{python}', '-c', <write one json file into argv[1]>, '{scratch}'] finds nothing: the placeholder expanded to a working interpreter and the scratch path arrived
the same testing runner with 'testing-no-such-interpreter' as its first word reds exactly once, with an exit value that starts 'un-runnable'

decisions.text: D1: the argv comprehension in a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail expands '{python}' to sys.executable beside '{scratch}'.

D2: the rehearsal row's drive in runners_leave_trails.json begins with '{python}'; the tester row is untouched. (The file sits at sieves/runners_leave_trails.json on main until 39eccfbc09aa lands; this ticket builds on that branch.)
D3: the proof test_a_runner_drive_runs_the_callers_interpreter.py, one tooth per falsifier clause, measuring only build_inspector.

out: cairn/machines/rehearsal/ (its CLI verb already leaves a trail; only the interpreter launching it was wrong)

measured.saw: test_a_failed_run_is_counted.py RED 3/4 on clean main ba93cd143 and on sieve-why-39eccfbc09aa: finding a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail on rehearsal, exit 9009 (Windows Store python3 stub).
measured.how: python cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_a_failed_run_is_counted.py, run singly on akiendell (Windows 11), from the repo root
